title: Matched Hermes built-in memory versus HADES Hindsight memory gateway probe
classification: one synthetic local paired probe; no owner preference or release qualification

tracked_legacy_pair_replay.result: PASS; current overlay used canonical subject bank fallback, persisted a natural correction, and returned latest value on fresh typoed recall.
limitations: Disposable service/volume and synthetic extraction endpoint; no latency qualification or owner preference.
The runtime is Hermes 0.21.2 for this compatibility check, while the paired local gateway comparison uses Hermes 0.21.5.

interpretation.plain_preference: PLAIN native memory worked and produced shorter model-written recall. Save/correction each required a memory-tool model turn plus a response generation; fresh memory context was loaded at the next session.
interpretation.hades_preference: HADES explicit memory stayed within the authenticated subject bank and completed saves, correction, and typoed fresh recall without model or tool work. Gateway latency was lower in this single matched synthetic run.
interpretation.preference_bucket: UNASSIGNED; no Scotty dogfood or human naturalness review

pre_fix_correction_failure.meaning: HADES sounded as if it accepted the correction but had not changed persistent memory.

comparability_caveats: One sequential pair only; PLAIN ran first, so model/service warm state and order may influence timing.

Both use the same local model, runtime, hardware, request reasoning setting, and nominal context; HADES fast explicit memory deliberately bypasses the model, while PLAIN relies on its native memory tool.

The HADES correction route was initially not handled: 'Correction: ...' fell through to a model response and left mango unchanged. Added bounded subject-local correction detection, requiring at least two meaningful overlapping words with an existing tagged memory. The paired final run was after that fix.
A single synthetic preference does not establish owner preference, ordinary-chat quality, broad memory recall quality, or production latency.
not_qualified: No repeated paired run or counterbalanced order.
No real-model Hindsight extraction on HADES explicit writes; native chunks avoids extraction by design.
No owner preference, broader corpus, populated-data migration, production authentication, or Open WebUI route.
